records.real_world_identity_notes: The RaceRoom telemetry name matches the existing simulator-independent Porsche 963 record. The real car is Porsche's LMDh prototype, built by Porsche and Multimatic for the 2023 endurance-racing class, not the later road-oriented 963 RSP one-off. Porsche's specification identifies a seven-speed racing transmission and CFK racing clutch; Xtrac identifies the common LMDh P1359 as a seven-speed sequential gearbox. The reviewed sources establish wheel-mounted paddle and clutch controls, but do not establish the driver's complete launch, upshift, downshift, throttle-lift, cut, or blip technique for every competition configuration.

records.specification_basis: Porsche specifies a 7-speed racing transmission and Xtrac specifies the LMDh P1359 as 7 speed. Xtrac explicitly calls the P1359 a 7 speed sequential gearbox; Porsche's exact 963 specification independently identifies the seven-speed pneumatically actuated racing transmission. The official Porsche Motorsport North America explanation says the rear paddles upshift and downshift the 963, and contemporaneous reporting corroborates regular gearshift paddles at the rear of the wheel. Xtrac explicitly identifies the gearbox as sequential, and Porsche's official explanation describes paddle-operated upshift/downshift commands rather than a gear gate. The exact Porsche 963 cockpit photograph shows a fixed molded control wheel with dedicated left and right grips and a control face between them, so the hands stay at the grips; this is gt-formula rather than a continuous round or D-shaped band. The exact 963 cockpit photograph visibly includes a central digital display, and contemporaneous reporting identifies a color display on the wheel. Contemporaneous reporting on the Porsche 963 wheel explicitly states that shift lights and warning lights run across the top of the wheel. The photograph establishes a gt-formula fixed-grip control wheel rather than a continuous rim for which open-top geometry would be a separate property; the project's representation is therefore not-applicable. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
